key_insight: A measurement-free protocol uses coherent control of three superconducting cavities to correct photon loss and extend a binomial-encoded qubit’s lifetime beyond break-even in simulations.
engineering_relevance: Correcting dominant photon-loss errors locally could reduce the error-correction burden on an outer code in superconducting quantum computers.
method: Encode one logical qubit in a cavity’s lowest-order binomial code.
Use two ancillary cavities and Josephson-junction-based nonlinear couplings for coherent, measurement-free correction.
Optimize the waiting time between correction rounds.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations with experimentally realistic parameters report 99% single-photon-loss correction fidelity and a 1.2–1.8× logical lifetime relative to unprotected {|0⟩, |1⟩} Fock encoding.
watch_item: The results are simulation-based; experimental implementation must preserve sufficient coherent-control fidelity to retain the predicted lifetime advantage.
paper_title: A measurement-free quantum error correction protocol for superconducting cavities
